finding: Disrupting Education? Experimental Evidence on Technology-Aided Instruction in India
design: Individual randomized controlled trial: voucher lottery; intention-to-treat effect of the offer.
value: 619; grades 6–9 and 4–5: manuscript p. 9 and footnote 9 | 4.5 months: abstract and pp. 8–10 | 45+45 minutes: pp. 7–8 | 58%: p. 9 | 0.37 and 0.23 baseline SD: Table 2 p. 38

finding: A Meta-Analysis of the Effectiveness of Intelligent Tutoring Systems on K–12 Students’ Mathematical Learning

sample_scope: 26 reports and 34 independent samples, K–12 mathematics; only three elementary-school studies, from one research team. Unique combined participant N: NR here.
locator: pp. 971–975 (reports, samples, comparisons); p. 976 (overall models); Tables 2–3 pp. 977 and 979 (duration, achievement, grades); pp. 978–979 (elementary studies); p. 983 (limitations).
limitations: Low-achiever samples had less favorable, negative estimates, contrasting with the lower-performer benefit in Maine ASSISTments. These are between-study comparisons, not proof that duration, prior achievement or teacher involvement caused the differences. Reviews may overlap other cards.
